question:
Each cell in the attached spreadsheet represents a plot of land. The color of the cell indicates who owns that plot. Green cells are plots owned by Earl Smith. Can Earl walk through every plot he owns (and no other plots) and return to his starting plot without backtracking? For this question, consider backtracking to be any instance where Earl would enter a plot of land he had already entered since leaving his starting plot.

mistake_reason: Spreadsheet_Expert produced a malformed, non-JSON structure with single quotes, trailing comma, tuple parentheses, and embedded conversational text. Critically, they added an unauthorized 'note' that changed the adjacency rule to include diagonals, violating the task constraints. This formatting error (FM-4.4) forced downstream parsing fallbacks and led the algorithm to build the wrong graph (8-neighbor instead of 4-neighbor), causing the team to incorrectly find a Hamiltonian cycle and answer 'Yes' instead of the ground truth 'No'.
